parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem:
The hydrocarbons **A**, $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}$, and **B**, $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8$, are both unbranched.

**A** does **not** decolourise bromine.

**B** decolourises bromine and shows geometrical isomerism.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
The hydrocarbon **A**, $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}$, has a branched isomer.

Suggest why unbranched **A** has a higher boiling point than its branched isomer.

parts.label: (a)(v)
parts.text:
Draw the mechanism of the reaction of **B** with bromine, $\text{Br}_2$.
Include all necessary charges, dipoles, lone pairs and curly arrows.

parts.label: (a)(vi)
parts.text: Explain the origin of the dipole on $\text{Br}_2$ in this mechanism.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
The alcohols **C** and **D** are isomers of each other with molecular formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$. Both isomers are branched.

When **C** is heated under reflux with acidified potassium dichromate(VI) no colour change is observed.

When **D** is heated under reflux with acidified potassium dichromate(VI) the colour of the mixture changes from orange to green and **E**, $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$, is produced.

**E** reacts with aqueous sodium carbonate to form carbon dioxide gas.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Write the equation for the reaction between **E** and aqueous sodium carbonate.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem:
The isomers **F** and **G**, $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$, both form an orange precipitate when reacted with 2,4-DNPH.

**F** is unbranched and reacts with alkaline aqueous iodine to produce a yellow precipitate.

**G** does not react with alkaline aqueous iodine. It contains a chiral centre and produces a silver mirror when warmed with Tollens' reagent.
parts.text: Name the yellow precipitate produced by the reaction between **F** and alkaline aqueous iodine.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Give the structural formula of **F** and of **G**.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Explain the meaning of the term *chiral centre*.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem:
**H** and **I** are isomers with molecular formula $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}_2$. The infra-red spectra of isomers **H** and **I** are shown.

{{figure:pdf_visual_03.png}}
parts.text: Identify the bonds responsible for the principal peaks above $1500\text{ cm}^{-1}$ in each spectrum.
